PFNP, which mimics the ability of FGF-1 to stimulate DNA synthesis, does not bind the FGF receptor and does not induce FGF receptor phosphorylation but does induce phosphorylation of ERKS/2 MAP kinas, and that the activity of PFNP correlates with phosphorylation of the ERK1/ 2 MAP kinases.
a permeable FGF1 nuclear localization sequence induces DNA synthesis independently, but not exclusively, of Ras.

the membrane-permeable fibroblast growth factors-1 nuclear localization signal peptide PFNP stimulates DNA synthesis independently of FGF-1 receptor binding and Ras activation but requires ERK1/ERK2 activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel peptide that can be used as a tool to investigate the molecular mechanism of Ras-independent DNA synthesis and as an alternative to FGF-1 for the treatment of ischemia and other diseases.
the molecular basis for the ability of a permeable nuclear localization sequence peptide to stimulate DNA synthesis independently of FGF receptor activation.

the identification of the signaling pathways involved in PFNP-induced DNA replication, which may provide a clue to the mechanism by which FGF-1 exerts its mitogenic effect in a cell density-dependent manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PFNP induces DNA synthesis in murine fibrobasts independently of Ras, but through activation of tyrosines and ERK1 kinases.
PFNP-induced DNA syntheses are Ras independent and are not mediated by the FGF receptor but rather by tyrosine and ERK1 and ERK2 kinases.
PFNP induces DNA synthesis by activating a tyrosine- and ERK-dependent pathway independent of the FGF receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PFNP induces DNA synthesis independently from FGF receptor signaling, but that PFNP and the FGF-1 receptor system share the same signaling pathways at optimum cell density.

the nuclear localization signal (NLS) peptide of FGF-1 can induce DNA synthesis by an NLS-dependent, Ras-independent, FGF receptor-independent, tyrosine kinase-dependent, and ERK1 and ERK2 MAP kinase-dependent pathway.

the FGF-1 NLS peptide PFNP can mimic the mitogenic activity of FGF-1 at low cell densities, and that the underlying mechanism involves activation of tyrosin kinases and ERKS MAP kinases independently of Ras.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PFNP is a novel, cell-permeable, Ras-independent, tyrosine kinase-dependent, ERK1/ 2 kinase-dependent peptide that mimics the DNA synthetic activity of FGF-1 and that can be used for further elucidating Ras-independent signaling mechanisms.
PFNP is a useful tool for studying the Ras-independent FGF-1 mitogenic pathway.

PFNP, a cell-permeable FGF- 1 nuclear localization sequence (NLS) peptide, induces DNA synthesis through a signaling pathway that is independent of FGF-1 receptor tyrosine kinase activation and Ras, but dependent on ERK1/ 2 MAP kinase phosphorylations.
